messages:
Alex W: FYI — BetaCorp called in: SSO started failing right after they rotated IdP certs. They see a redirect loop and our logs show ACS mismatch.
Priya R: ugh. do we have their metadata? any duplicate entityID or weird ACS ordering?
Alex W: they sent the metadata blob. i pasted a snippet below — looks like two EntityDescriptor blocks with the same entityID but differing ACS lists. customer says one IdP was decommissioned but metadata still has both.
Alex W: ```xml
<md:EntitiesDescriptor>
  <md:EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.betacorp.com">
    <md:SPSSODescriptor>
      <md:AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST" Location="https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs" index="1" isDefault="true"/>
    </md:SPSSODescriptor>
  </md:EntityDescriptor>
  <!-- old, decommissioned but still present -->
  <md:EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.betacorp.com">
    <md:SPSSODescriptor>
      <md:AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://legacy.betacorp.com/sso/acs" index="0"/>
    </md:SPSSODescriptor>
  </md:EntityDescriptor>
</md:EntitiesDescriptor>
```
Jordan M: that duplicate entityID is a problem — our metadata parser expects unique entityIDs. if the IdP advertises multiple descriptors with the same entityID, some XML consumers pick the first one and ignore the rest, which can cause the ACS URL we validate against to mismatch.
Tim S: logs from auth-service show: 
```
ERROR saml: received AssertionConsumerService URL https://legacy.betacorp.com/sso/acs not present in configured ACS list for SP https://app.redwood.ai
WARN saml: possible duplicate EntityDescriptor for idp entityID=https://idp.betacorp.com; using first match
```
Priya R: ok. two fronts: 1) immediate mitigation so customer can log in; 2) long-term guidance. for immediate: ask their IdP admin to remove the duplicate EntityDescriptor or re-generate metadata to only include the active IdP entity. if they can't, have them ensure the ACS list in the first entityDescriptor includes our ACS (https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs) and set isDefault properly.
Alex W: we also accept manual ACS entries in the org settings — can add the legacy ACS to the allowed list temporarily?
Jordan M: we can, but that risks accepting a redirect to a non-expected endpoint. safer is to whitelist exactly https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs and tell them to collapse duplicate descriptors. if they insist on keeping both entries, we can add a special-case relaxation for this org for 24h while they fix metadata, but it needs approval.
Priya R: propose steps to customer (short):
- re-export IdP metadata, ensure only a single EntityDescriptor for https://idp.betacorp.com
- verify AssertionConsumerService list contains https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs and that isDefault is correct
- if they rotated certs, ensure new KeyDescriptor (signing) is present and not duplicated with old certs in a way that confuses selection
- send metadata back for quick check
Alex W: i've drafted a message to BetaCorp with those steps and asking for the fresh metadata. also asked for the exact time they rotated certs. sending now.
SRE Bot: deploy-notify: checked recent deploys — no platform changes to saml parser in last 7 days.
Tim S: once we get their fixed metadata i can validate locally with samltool and run a test SAML response. if they need a short-lived workaround, we can open a config ticket to add the legacy ACS URL to allowed endpoints for their org, mark as temporary, and document expiration.
Jordan M: note: cert rotation race can also happen if metadata contains both old and new KeyDescriptor entries and IdP rotates ordering mid-assertion. recommend they avoid overlapping metadata with both active keys unless necessary.
Priya R: assigning follow-up to me. i'll coordinate with customer, validate returned metadata, and loop Jordan/Tim for validation. Alex — can you CC the account manager so they know we're on it?
Alex W: done. cc'd AM.
Priya R: next update in this thread after we get metadata back. :thumbsup:
